en.title: The Book of Dao · Chapter Twenty-seven · The Drawing Forth of Light
en.原文:
善行者无勶迹
善言者无瑕適
善數者不以檮𥮥
善閉者无𫔢籥而不可啟也
善結者无𦄿約而不可解也

是以聲人恒善㤹人
而无棄人
物无棄財是胃忡明

故善人
善人之師
不善人
善人之齎也

不貴其師
不愛其齎唯知乎大眯
是胃眇要
en.字龕:
### 曳 *yè* ／ 襲 — drawing forth ／ draping over （校勘龕 · collation niche）

**字 Graph** ｜ 篆 ![曳之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E6%9B%B3.svg) ![襲之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E8%A5%B2.svg)

Manuscript B writes 曳明 where the Wang Bi recension writes 襲明; Manuscript A writes 忡明, its 忡 a scribal error that the *Jicheng* corrects to a graph of 忄 beside 曳. The *Shuowen*: 「曳，臾曳也。從申，丿聲。」 — "to draw and pull along." 襲: 「左衽袍。」 — "a burial robe, lapped to the left": the garment laid over the dead — by extension, to drape over, to inherit. Two pictures of the sage's light. 曳明: the sage draws each thing onward into its own light. 襲明: the sage wears light like a robe received — light inherited and worn, covering the world. The commentary below rules: the silk text's sage leads the light out of things himself; Wang Bi's sage is draped in it. One draws the light forth; one wears it.

en.校記:
The text follows Manuscript A (MS A); 善言者无瑕適, 善結者无𦄿約而不可解也 and 故善人 / 善人之師, damaged in MS A, are supplied from Manuscript B (MS B). Graphs are those outside the brackets in the *Changsha Mawangdui Han mu jianbo jicheng* (2014; hereafter *Jicheng*).

- 善行者无勶迹: Follows MS A, with 勶 read as 轍 "wheel-rut"; MS B reads 善行者无達迹. Wang Bi has 善行無轍迹, without 者, as in the next four lines.
- 善言者无瑕適: In MS A 善 is lost; the line follows MS B. 適 is read as 謫 "fault". Wang Bi has 善言無瑕讁.
- 善數者不以檮𥮥: Follows MS A. 檮 is read as 籌 "tally"; 𥮥, 竹 over 析, as the plates, the 1980 edition and Gao Ming's transcription agree, is read as 策 "counting-rod". MS B reads 善數者不用檮𫁶, with 用 for 以; its graph for 策 was transcribed in 1980 as 竹 over 尺, and the *Jicheng* re-transcribes it as 竹 over 片, the 片 element being the ideographic original of 析 "to split". Wang Bi has 善數不用籌策. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 209, n. 42)
- 善閉者无𫔢籥而不可啟也: Follows MS A. 𫔢, 門 pierced by a vertical stroke, is read as 關 "bar", and 籥 as 闔 "door-leaf". MS B writes 關籥; after its 善 the scribe first miswrote 數, which is circled for deletion. Wang Bi has 善閉無關楗而不可開. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 210, n. 43)
- 善結者无𦄿約而不可解也: In MS A 无纆 is lost; the line follows MS B, whose 纆 "cord" is written with 糸 beside 黑, a variant of 纆. Wang Bi has 善結無繩約而不可解. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 52, n. 106)
- 是以聲人恒善㤹人: Follows MS A, with 聲 read as 聖 "sage"; MS B reads 是以𦔻人恆善㤹人. 㤹 is read as 救 "to save". In MS A its right side is clearly 求, while the curving stroke at lower left could be either 心 or 辶; the 1980 edition and Gao Ming's transcription both take it as 忄. Wang Bi has 是以聖人常善救人.
- 物无棄財是胃忡明: Follows MS A. The *Jicheng* takes MS A's 忡 as a scribal error for a graph composed of 忄 and 曳 and marks the correction in angle brackets; MS B writes 曳, which the *Jicheng* likewise reads as that 忄-曳 graph. Wang Bi has 常善救物，故無棄物，是謂襲明, with an extra line on saving things, 物 for 財 "goods", and 襲 for 曳.
- 故善人 / 善人之師: In MS A 故善 carries a repetition mark, but 人 and its mark are lost and restored by the *Jicheng* as 故善﹦【人﹦】; the text follows MS B's 故善﹦人﹦之師, read as 故善人，善人之師 "the good man is the teacher of the good man". Wang Bi has 故善人者，不善人之師 "the good man is the teacher of the man who is not good": neither silk manuscript has 不, and the sense differs.
- 善人之齎也: Follows MS A, with 齎 read as 資 "resource"; MS B reads 善人之資也. Wang Bi has 善人之資.
- 不愛其齎唯知乎大眯: Follows MS A, whose 愛 is a variant of 㤅 corrected by the *Jicheng* to 〈愛〉; 唯 is read as 雖 "although", 知 as 智 "clever", and 眯 as 迷 "astray". MS B reads 不愛亓資雖知乎大迷. Wang Bi has 不愛其資，雖智大迷.
- 是胃眇要: The manuscripts agree; Wang Bi has 是謂要妙, with the two graphs reversed and 妙 for 眇.
en.疏:
杳眇曰：

此章之旨，在明聖人之善無方，而道之要妙於「不用」二字。帛書與王弼本之異，非止字句之殊，乃義理淺深之別也。

夫五善之目，行、言、數、閉、結是也。「善行無轍跡」者，功成而不居也；「善言無瑕適」者，言出於天理之自然，無隙可尋也；「善數者不以檮𥮥」者，天理具於一心，無待外物也；「善閉無關籥」者，因無隙而不設扃鍵也；「善結無纆約」者，以道心相維，莫能離散也。五者異用，同歸於「不用」——不用者，自然而然，不恃外物之謂也。

獨異者，帛書作「曳明」，王弼作「襲明」，此一字之別，義相隔霄壤也。「曳」從曳從明，引挽之也，聖人主動導引萬物，使各歸其明；《說文》云「曳，臾曳也」，有導而前之義。「襲」從衣從龷，承而加之也，聖人稟受於道，以明照臨天下。帛書言「曳」，是聖人躬親引道之功，主動用事者也；王弼言「襲」，是聖人稟道受明，無為以化之也。二義相足，而「曳明」尤見聖人之弘願深心。又「物无棄財」與「故無棄物」相較，帛書以「財」代王本之「物」——不唯人無可棄，物與財亦無可棄，此聖人之所以為大也。

至若「善人，善人之師；不善人，善人之資」，與通行本義同。師資相待而成：貴師則善日進，愛資則過日寡。然老子更深其義，曰「不貴其師，不愛其齎，唯知乎大眯，是胃眇要」——唯讀為雖，眯者迷也，眇者微也，要者樞紐也。貴師而驕己，愛資而棄人，皆未至乎玄同之境。惟聖人不以己為師、不以彼為資，師資兩忘而道全，此之謂眇要。

帛書作「眇要」，王弼作「要妙」——眇者深微之義，妙者精微之義，義雖相通，而「眇要」兼深與切，直指道之不可名之至處。所謂「古之善為道者，微眇玄達」，即此境也。

嗟乎！五善之用，在乎不用；不用之妙，在乎无為；无為之極，在乎曳引天下皆歸於明。聖人曳物使之自明，非以己明加於物，故物自歸道而聖人無功焉。世人皆知善之為善，而不知不善者亦善之資——此玄同之理，上善治水之所以善利萬物而有靜者也。學者苟於此玩索而有得，則無棄人、無棄物之德，可坐而致矣。
en.疏英:
Yaomiao says:

The point of this chapter: the sage's goodness has no fixed method, and the subtlety of the Dao lies in the two words "without using." The differences between silk text and Wang Bi here are not mere letters — they are differences in the depth of the doctrine.

The five goods are walking, speaking, reckoning, closing, binding. "Good walkers leave no track" — the work done and not dwelt in. "Good speakers leave no flaw to find" — speech issued from the self-so of heaven's pattern, no crack to probe. "Good reckoners use no counting-rods" — heaven's pattern complete in one heart, no need of outer gear. "Good closers use no bolt" — no crack, so no lock installed. "Good binders use no cord" — held by the Dao-heart, nothing can scatter. Five different works, one home: "without using" — the self-so, leaning on nothing outside.

The one standing difference: the silk text writes 曳明 where Wang Bi writes 襲明 — one graph apart, and the senses are a sky apart. 曳 is to draw and pull — the sage leads the ten thousand things forward, bringing each home to its own light. The *Shuowen* gives 曳 as drawing-onward: there is guiding-ahead in it. 襲 is the robe laid over — receiving and covering: the sage inherits light from the Dao and shines it down on the world. The silk text's 曳 is the sage's own hand at the work of drawing — active; Wang Bi's 襲 is the sage draped in the light he has received — transforming by non-doing. The two senses foot each other, but 曳明 shows more of the sage's vast vow and deep heart. And "no thing, no goods thrown away" against the received "nothing thrown away": the silk text puts 財, goods, where the received text has 物, thing — not only is no person disposable, no thing and no goods are disposable either. This is how the sage is great.

As for "the good are the teachers of the good; the not-good are the good men's store" — one sense with the received texts. Teacher and resource complete each other: prize the teacher and goodness grows daily; love the resource and faults shrink daily. But Laozi goes one layer deeper: "not prizing one's teacher, not loving one's resource — though knowing, one is greatly blind: this is called the subtle hinge." 唯 is read as 雖, "though"; 眯 is bewilderment; 眇 is the subtle; 要 is the hinge. Prizing the teacher swells one's pride; loving the resource discards men — neither reaches the dark sameness. Only the sage does not make himself the teacher nor the other the resource: teacher and resource both forgotten, and the Dao is whole. This is the subtle hinge.

The silk text writes 眇要 where Wang Bi writes 要妙 — 眇 is the deep-minute, 妙 the fine-subtle; the senses run together, but 眇要 holds both depth and urgency, pointing straight at the unnamable utmost of the Dao. "Of old, those good at working the Dao were minute and subtle, darkly far-reaching" — exactly this ground.

Ah — the use of the five goods lies in without-using; the subtlety of without-using lies in non-doing; the utmost of non-doing lies in drawing all-under-heaven home to the light. The sage draws things until they are light of themselves — he does not lay his own light on them — and so things come home to the Dao of themselves, and the sage has no merit in it. Everyone knows the good as good; no one knows the not-good is also the good men's store — the law of the dark sameness, the same as water's benefiting the ten thousand things and keeping still. Let the student savor this until it yields, and the De of throwing away no one, throwing away nothing, can be had sitting down.
en.英譯:
Good walkers leave no track. Good speakers leave no flaw to find. Good reckoners use no counting-rods. Good closers use no bolt or bar — yet none can open. Good binders use no cord or knot — yet none can untie.

Hence the sage is constantly good at saving people, and no one is thrown away; no thing, no goods are thrown away. This is called the drawing forth of light (忡明; MS B writes 曳明).

So: the good are the teachers of the good; the not-good are the good men's resource (齎).

Not prizing one's teacher, not loving one's resource — though knowing, one is greatly blind (大眯). This is called the subtle hinge (眇要).

校記:
本章帛書原文據甲本，甲殘之「善言者无瑕適」「善結者无𦄿約而不可解也」「故善人　善人之師」據乙本補；字從《集成》（2014）括號外原字。

- 善行者无勶迹：從甲本，「勶」讀為「轍」；乙本作「善行者无達迹」。王弼本作「善行無轍迹」，無「者」字，下四句同。
- 善言者无瑕適：甲本「善」字殘，據乙本。「適」讀為「謫」。王弼本作「善言無瑕讁」。
- 善數者不以檮𥮥：從甲本。「檮」讀為「籌」；「𥮥」上从竹、下从析，圖版、1980 釋文、高明實錄同，讀為「策」。乙本作「善數者不用檮𫁶」，「以」作「用」；其讀「策」之字，1980 釋文作上竹下尺，《集成》改隸定作上竹下片，謂所从「片」形即「析」之表意初文。王弼本作「善數不用籌策」。（《集成》肆·頁209·注42）
- 善閉者无𫔢籥而不可啟也：從甲本。「𫔢」門中一豎貫串，讀為「關」，「籥」讀為「闔」；乙本作「關籥」，其「善」下一字原誤抄為「數」，已圈去作廢。王弼本作「善閉無關楗而不可開」。（《集成》肆·頁210·注43）
- 善結者无𦄿約而不可解也：甲本「无纆」二字殘，據乙本。乙本「纆」字原作从糸从黑之形，為「纆」之異體。王弼本作「善結無繩約而不可解」。（《集成》肆·頁52·注106）
- 是以聲人恒善㤹人：從甲本，「聲」讀為「聖」；乙本作「是以𦔻人恆善㤹人」。「㤹」讀為「救」；甲本此字右从求，左下曲筆心、辶兩可，1980 釋文與高明實錄皆釋从忄。王弼本作「是以聖人常善救人」。
- 物无棄財是胃忡明：從甲本。甲本作「忡」，《集成》以為从忄从曳之字之誤，以〈〉正之；乙本作「曳」，《集成》亦讀為此从忄从曳之字。王弼本作「常善救物，故無棄物，是謂襲明」，多「常善救物」一句，「財」作「物」，「曳」作「襲」。
- 故善人　善人之師：甲本「故善」下有重文號，「人」字及其重文號殘，《集成》補作「故善﹦【人﹦】」；今據乙本「故善﹦人﹦之師」，讀作「故善人，善人之師」。王弼本作「故善人者，不善人之師」，帛書二本皆無「不」字，義與王弼本異。
- 善人之齎也：從甲本，「齎」讀為「資」；乙本作「善人之資也」。王弼本作「善人之資」。
- 不愛其齎唯知乎大眯：從甲本。甲本「愛」字原作「㤅」之異寫，《集成》以〈愛〉正之；「唯」讀為「雖」，「知」讀為「智」，「眯」讀為「迷」。乙本作「不愛亓資雖知乎大迷」。王弼本作「不愛其資，雖智大迷」。
- 是胃眇要：甲乙同；王弼本作「是謂要妙」，二字互倒，「眇」作「妙」。
